sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C. V. Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.16843 of 2024
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioner, seeking the following relief:
"....to issue appropriate writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ declaring the action of the respondents No.4 in not considering objections submitted by the petitioners on 27-09-2023 and 09-09-2022 in respect of land in Sy No 205, 265, 307, 358, 361 and 366 of Itikyala Village, Jagdevpur Mandal, Siddipet District and in issuing notification No.S. No.3553(E), dt 08-08-2023 issued by the Respondent No.2 under Section 3 D of the National High Way Act as illegal, arbitrary against principles of natural justice and against Article 300-A of Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents to consider the objections submitted by the petitioners on 22-09-2023 and 09-09-2022 in respect of land in lands in Sy. No.205, 265, 307, 358,
361 and 366 of Itikyala Village, Jagdevpur Mandal. Siddipet District ..."
2. The petitioners claim to have succeeded lands in various Survey Numbers forming part of Itikyala Village, Jagadevpur Mandal, Siddipet District, from their father Late Hanmantha Rao.

It is the case of the petitioners that previously the said lands were classified as Ceiling Surplus lands as per the orders of the Original Authority under the provisions of the Land Reforms Act and subsequently, in Appeal vide CC No.G/978/75, dated 22.06.1984, the orders passed by the Original Authority were modified and lands in certain survey numbers were released in favor of the petitioners.

Thereafter,
the revenue authorities recognized the petitioners as pattedars and possessors of the lands in question, vide Letter No.B/353/2018 dated 28.05.2018.

While the matter stood thus, the respondent No.2 issued Notification vide SO No.3993(E) dated 23.08.2022 under Section 3A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956, indicating the acquisition of specific lands for the purpose of constructing Regional Ring Road.
It is further stated that the petitioners raised objections stating that their claims concerning several survey numbers are pending for resolution before the revenue authorities.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that the name of their father was recorded as possessor in respect of lands admeasuring 4 acres in Sy.No.205, 0.36 1/3 gts in Sy.No.265, 4 acres 5 1/4 gts in Sy.No.307, 11 acres in Sy.No.358, 5 acres 32 1/4 gts in Sy.No.361 and 20 acres 19 gts in Sy.No.366 and while some portions of their lands have been released in their favor, several claims remained unresolved and they have made representations to the concerned authorities.

It is further case of the petitioners that they filed Writ Petition No.44661 of 2022 on the file of this Court and this Court disposed of said writ petition vide order dated 13.12.2022, directing the respondent No.3 to consider the objections raised by petitioners dated 09.09.2022 and pass appropriate orders Kiran Kumar Itikala vs The Ministry Of Road Transport And ... on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63308308/
1 thereon and communicate the same to the petitioners before further proceeding in the matter.

sentences.text: Inspite of the said order, the respondent No.2 issued Notification No.3553 dated 08-08- 2023 under Section 3D of the National Highways Act, without adequately addressing the objections raised by the petitioners.

It is further case of the petitioners that the respondents No.4 also issued notification under Section 3-G (3) of N.H.Act vide Letter No.B/467/2022, dated 26.08.2023 to hear the claims relating to the Jagadevpur Mandal and fixed the date on 27.09.2023, wherein the petitioners have attended and submitted their objections.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that even though the respondents have received the objections dated 27.09.2023 submitted by the petitioners, till date they are not considering the same and awarding compensation as per the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ("RFCTLARR Act").

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned counsel prays this Court to direct the respondents to consider the objections submitted by the petitioners on 27.09.2023 to the respondent No.4 by allowing the writ petition as prayed for.

4. Per contra, the learned Standing Counsel for NHAI would submit that the respondents have taken note of the objections submitted by the petitioners and the competent authority will pass appropriate orders, in accordance with law.

It is further submitted that if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority would refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

5. In view of the above submissions, as it is stated that the petitioners have submitted objections vide representation dated 27.09.2023 to the respondent No.4, this Court, without going into the merits of the case, deems it appropriate to direct the respondent No.4 to examine the objections submitted by the petitioners vide representation dated 27.09.2023 and pass appropriate orders, in accordance with law.
6. Accordingly, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
No order as to costs.

_ _ C.V. BHASKAR REDDY, J Date: 11.09.2024 scs Kiran Kumar Itikala vs The Ministry Of Road Transport And ... on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63308308/
